headline: Celtics hit four game skid while Bruins offense keeps rolling along
morning_brew: I haven't seen the C's struggle like this in five years, and losing a heartbreaker by one point to the Warriors on Sunday night is just the cherry on top of a brutal stretch. We had chances to put it away, but when the shots don't fall, you are just begging for trouble. Getting sent home with an 87-88 final score when you are fighting to find your rhythm is enough to make a guy walk the long way home from the Garden, maybe stopping at Dunks just to scream into a medium roast. It is time for the coaching staff to look in the mirror before this four-game slide turns into something even uglier.

On the flip side, the Bruins are absolutely electric right now, especially with Elias Lindholm putting on a show for the ages. Scoring four goals in a single night to carry us past the Capitals in a 7-5 victory is exactly the kind of performance that reminds you why we love this game. When a guy like Lindholm takes over like that, it lifts the whole room, and I am just hoping the boys can keep that momentum going when they return to the ice later this week. That level of offensive production is wicked, and it is a massive breath of fresh air for a team that desperately needed a spark.

Over in the NFL, the Patriots are in a tough spot after the news that Mike Vrabel is sticking with Tommy DeVito as the starter while Drake Maye heals from his fractured fibula. It is a massive blow to the offense, and frankly, we are all just hoping DeVito can keep us competitive in these next few weeks. I am looking for any sign that the game plan is moving in the right direction, but until we see it on the field, I will be sitting here waiting for some good news out of the facility while neighbor Rick tries to convince me it's all part of a deeper government conspiracy.

news_digest.headline: Vrabel: Patriots sticking with DeVito as QB1, not looking for outside help
news_digest.dans_take: Losing Maye for weeks is a total gut punch that has me questioning my entire Sunday routine.
